title: Held commit (the promotion lane)
description: A commit that is finished but deliberately NOT live yet, because it belongs to a class of change that must be rebuilt, re-indexed or re-materialized and proven before it ships. Without this record 'held' means a commit in somebody's local worktree: no age, no owner, invisible to the board, and gone when the worktree is cleaned. A held record names the sha, why it is held, what must be proven before it can go live, and who holds it -- so it ages in public and is promoted with evidence rather than forgotten.

title.description: One line a reader can act on: repo, short sha and the subject.

repo.description: The project path a reader can fetch from, e.g. team/budget-app.

sha.description: The held commit. It must exist on a ref a reader can fetch; a commit only in one worktree is what this record exists to prevent.

branch.description: The ref it was parked on, e.g. `staging`.

reason.description: Why it may not go live yet, in the holder's own words.

rebuild.description: What must be rebuilt, re-indexed or re-materialized -- and PROVEN -- before this can go live. Nothing to rebuild means it was never a held-class change.

reachable.description: How the sha was proven fetchable: attested by the client that holds the repo (a remote branch contains it), confirmed by the Hub's own commit resolver (a remote-tracking ref, or the configured forge resolver, contains it -- never mere existence in a local checkout), or both. `unpushed` is the recorded exception -- the commit exists on ONE DISK and the record says why it could not be parked anywhere safe.

unpushed_reason.description: Why this commit is on no remote. Required when reachable is `unpushed`: the alternative is a hold that looks exactly like a safe one while being one deleted directory from gone. A repository can legitimately have nowhere safe to park a commit (a push to any branch triggers a job against production, say).

hub_saw.description: What the Hub itself found when the hold was recorded, kept even when the client attestation carried it through: `local_only` means the commit was present in a checkout the Hub can read and contained in NO remote-tracking ref there. Existence on a disk is not fetchability.

local_path.description: The directory the unpushed commit exists in, so a reader can go and get it.

from_gap.description: The gap this hold answers. Before a fix is a commit the honest record is an OPEN GAP; the commit can arrive days later, and naming the gap keeps the queue and the Gaps tab telling ONE story.

promoted_note.description: The rebuild that actually ran, with its counts.

allOf.description: A promotion is a claim about production, so it carries the evidence that it ran -- the same rule a gap obeys when it calls itself closed.
Abandoning held work is a decision, and a decision states its reason.
A commit on no remote is allowed, never silently: it says why, so the exception is a recorded decision rather than an accident that reads as fine.
